metaDescription: Five Reizen talking clocks compared, from the one-button Extra Large model to atomic and cube styles, with setup, voice and buying advice.
introParagraphs: Reizen is one of the few brands that has built a whole product line around speaking the time out loud. Its clocks range from a plain one-button puck to atomic models that correct themselves from a radio signal, so the right choice depends far more on how the person will use it than on which looks nicest.

We evaluated five distinct Reizen models based on product specs and the feature lists in each listing. We grouped them by how the time is set, how many things the clock can announce, and how simple the controls are for someone who just wants to press and listen.

Language variants, such as the Spanish version of the Extra Large Button clock, are the same hardware with a different voice, so they are covered in the buying advice rather than counted as separate picks.

products.name: Reizen Talking Atomic Alarm Clock
products.description:
The Reizen Talking Atomic Alarm Clock pairs a full-range female voice with an atomic time source, so the time it speaks is corrected for you instead of drifting week by week. It announces the time and date on request and changes for daylight saving time on its own. That removes the twice-yearly resetting chore that trips up so many households with a basic clock.

An optional hourly announcement runs from 8am to 10pm, which suits someone who likes to hear the hour pass without reaching for a button. The voice is female, and some listeners with high-pitched hearing loss find lower voices clearer, so it is worth hearing a sample before gifting it. This is a clock for people who value accuracy and a gentle daytime chime more than a pocket-sized gadget.

In daily use it sits on a table or nightstand and asks for little beyond fresh power, so check the listing for the supply type before you buy. Next to the Reizen Extra Large Button Talking Alarm Clock at 3.50 inches across, this model is a fuller desk clock rather than a single-button puck. It also handles daylight saving automatically, which the Reizen Talking LCD Alarm Cube Clock does not list.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants a talking clock that never needs resetting and can announce the hour on its own.

Full-range voice reads time and date on request
cons: Female voice may be harder for some hearing losses
Hourly announcements can bother light sleepers

products.name: Reizen Extra Large Button Talking Alarm Clock
products.description:
The Reizen Extra Large Button Talking Alarm Clock is the simplest clock in the lineup. A big white button sits in a compact black base, and pressing it announces the time and date in a clear English-speaking voice. The whole unit measures 3.50 inches across and 1.25 inches high, so it fits on a crowded nightstand or in a travel bag.

Four low-profile non-slip feet keep it flat and steady while you press, which matters because a clock that slides away from your hand is frustrating for someone who cannot see it. The tradeoff is that there is no display to speak of in the listing, so the voice is the only way to read the time. People who also want a glanceable face for visitors or caregivers should look at the cube models instead.

Setup is the main thing to plan for, since you will want a helper nearby for the first time and alarm setting. Compared with the Reizen Talking Atomic Alarm Clock, this one is far smaller and has fewer features, but there is less to learn and nothing to misread. A Spanish version with a red button shares the same 3.50 by 1.25 inch body if the listener prefers Spanish.
products.bestFor: People who want one big button, a clear voice and almost nothing else to learn.

products.name: Reizen Talking Atomic Analog Alarm Clock
products.description:
The Reizen Talking Atomic Analog Alarm Clock keeps a traditional clock face while adding speech. A single touch of the button announces the time, and a second touch gives the day and date. The time is set by a daily radio signal from an atomic clock, so the hands stay accurate without manual adjustment.

That combination suits someone who has always read an analog dial and does not want to give it up, but also needs the spoken backup. The touch button is less tactile than a raised physical one, so people with limited feeling in their fingertips should try it first. A 90-day warranty is stated in the listing, which is shorter than many buyers expect, so keep the receipt.

Placing it where the radio signal can reach matters, since a clock in a basement or beside large metal appliances may struggle to receive its daily update. Compared with the Reizen Talking Atomic Alarm Clock, this model trades the hourly announcement option for a dial face you can read at a glance. It is also quieter in feel than the Reizen Extra Large Button Talking Alarm Clock, which relies on a big physical button rather than a touch surface.
products.bestFor: Dial lovers who want an atomic clock that also speaks the time and date.

products.name: Reizen 3-in-1 Talking Super Cube Clock
products.description:
The Reizen 3-in-1 Talking Super Cube Clock does three jobs in one compact cube. It speaks the time, reads out a talking calendar, and runs a talking countdown timer, with a dual voice feature to choose how it sounds. For a person who cooks, takes pills on a schedule or likes to know the date, that is more useful than a time-only clock.

The extra functions are also the extra things to learn, so it suits someone comfortable pressing several buttons rather than one. The countdown timer is a practical detail for kitchen tasks, laundry or a short nap, and hearing it called out removes the need to read tiny digits. Buyers who only want to hear the time will pay for features they never touch.

Cube shapes sit well on a desk or kitchen counter, though a taller cube takes up more footprint than a flat puck. Compared with the Reizen Extra Large Button Talking Alarm Clock at 3.50 inches across, this cube offers three functions where that clock offers one. Next to the Reizen Talking LCD Alarm Cube Clock, it adds the timer and calendar but the listing does not mention the alarm being a headline feature.
products.bestFor: Cooks and organized users who want a talking timer and calendar along with the time.

Three functions fit in one compact cube
cons: More buttons to learn than the single-button pucks
Listing gives few details on alarm settings
Extra functions are wasted if you only need the time

products.name: Reizen Talking LCD Alarm Cube Clock
products.description:
The Reizen Talking LCD Alarm Cube Clock adds a modern LCD display to a speaking cube, so it works for the listener and for anyone who glances at it. The built-in alarm wakes you with either a beep or a voice, which is helpful because a spoken wake-up can feel gentler than a harsh buzzer. It is finished in silver and black and sits on a tabletop.

The LCD is easy to read at a glance for people with mild vision loss, though low-vision users should still lean on the voice rather than the digits. Because it pairs a screen with speech, it works well in a shared bedroom where a partner or caregiver wants to read the time without pressing anything. The limitation is that the listing says little about daylight saving handling or setup steps.

Check how the clock is powered and how the time is set before you commit, since the brief for this model does not spell those out. Compared with the Reizen Talking Atomic Alarm Clock, it lacks any listed atomic correction, so expect to adjust it by hand. It is simpler than the Reizen 3-in-1 Talking Super Cube Clock, which adds a calendar and a talking timer on top of the time.
products.bestFor: Shared bedrooms where both a spoken time and a readable screen are wanted.

Alarm can wake you with a beep or a voice
Cube shape sits steadily on a nightstand
Silver and black finish matches most bedroom decor
cons: No atomic or automatic daylight saving listed

buyingCriteria.explanation: The number of controls decides whether the clock is a daily comfort or a daily frustration. A single large button, like the one on the Reizen Extra Large Button Talking Alarm Clock, announces the time on the first press and the date on the second, which is the lowest learning load you can get. Multi-function clocks such as the Reizen 3-in-1 Talking Super Cube Clock give you a calendar and countdown timer but ask the user to remember which key does what. As a rule of thumb, if the person has trouble with a TV remote, choose the single-button style. Features should only be added when the user has a clear reason to want them.

Clocks that read a daily radio signal correct themselves, which stops the slow drift that makes a household clock wrong by several minutes over a season. The Reizen Talking Atomic Alarm Clock and the Reizen Talking Atomic Analog Alarm Clock both use this approach, and the first also changes for daylight saving on its own. Hand-set clocks need someone to adjust them twice a year in many regions, and a talking clock that announces the wrong hour confidently is worse than silence. If the user lives alone and nobody visits regularly, favor an atomic model. If a helper is always nearby, hand setting is fine and keeps the cost of ownership lower.

Hearing loss often affects higher frequencies first, so a sharp, high-pitched voice can be harder to understand than a lower one even at full volume. The Reizen Talking Atomic Alarm Clock uses a full-range female voice, while the Reizen Extra Large Button Talking Alarm Clock is described with a clear English-speaking voice and the Reizen 3-in-1 Talking Super Cube Clock offers a dual voice feature. A dual voice choice is the safest bet if you cannot test in person, because you can swap if the first voice does not suit. Always compare a spoken sample before gifting a clock to someone with known hearing loss.

A talking clock lives on a nightstand or kitchen counter, so footprint matters more than most buyers expect. The Reizen Extra Large Button Talking Alarm Clock measures just 3.50 inches in diameter and 1.25 inches high, which fits beside a lamp and a glass of water. Cube clocks such as the Reizen Talking LCD Alarm Cube Clock stand taller and take a squarer footprint, and the analog Reizen Talking Atomic Analog Alarm Clock needs room for a visible dial. Measure the space before you buy, and leave a clear spot the user can find by touch every time.

Many people buy a talking clock for the time announcement and forget to check how the alarm actually sounds. The Reizen Talking LCD Alarm Cube Clock lets you choose a beep or a voice, which is useful for sleepers who startle easily. Hourly announcements, like the optional 8am to 10pm option on the Reizen Talking Atomic Alarm Clock, can help during the day but may disturb sleep if the clock sits on a bedside table. If the listener wakes at the same time each day, a simple alarm is plenty. Otherwise look for a clock that offers a choice, so you can match the sound to how deeply the person sleeps.

Reizen sells the same body in different voice languages, so the model name alone does not tell you what you will hear. The Spanish version of the extra large button clock has a red button, shares the same 3.50 by 1.25 inch body and speaks with a Spanish-speaking voice, while the English listing at the same size has a white button. If the listener is bilingual or prefers Spanish, buy the matching language version rather than assuming the voice can be changed. Read the title carefully, since two near-identical listings can speak entirely different languages. A mismatch is the most common avoidable return with this brand.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ease of Operation
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how many presses it takes to hear the time and the date, and whether the controls can be found by touch. The Reizen Extra Large Button Talking Alarm Clock scores highest because one big button does the main job. The Reizen 3-in-1 Talking Super Cube Clock scores lower on simplicity because it packs a calendar and timer into the same body. This is based on product specs and listing details, not hands-on testing.

howWeEvaluated.title: Time Accuracy and Upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how each clock keeps its time and how much manual resetting it is likely to need. The Reizen Talking Atomic Alarm Clock leads because it uses an atomic source and changes for daylight saving automatically. The Reizen Talking Atomic Analog Alarm Clock also gets a daily radio signal, while the Reizen Talking LCD Alarm Cube Clock lists no such correction. Clocks that stay right without help rank higher for anyone living alone.

howWeEvaluated.title: Voice and Announcements
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered what each clock can say, from the plain time and date to calendar and countdown readouts. The Reizen 3-in-1 Talking Super Cube Clock offers the widest range, with a dual voice feature and a talking timer. The Reizen Talking Atomic Alarm Clock adds an optional hourly report from 8am to 10pm. The simplest models speak only on demand, which some buyers will prefer.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and Portability
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed footprint and travel friendliness, since many buyers want a clock for a nightstand and a bag. The Reizen Extra Large Button Talking Alarm Clock is the most portable at 3.50 inches across and 1.25 inches high. The cube models take more desk space, and the analog atomic clock needs room for its dial. Portability matters most for people who travel to see family.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup Positioning and Value
howWeEvaluated.description: We placed the five picks against one another to show where each one leads. The Reizen Talking Atomic Alarm Clock leads on accuracy and automation, the Reizen Extra Large Button Talking Alarm Clock on simplicity, and the Reizen 3-in-1 Talking Super Cube Clock on feature count. The Reizen Talking Atomic Analog Alarm Clock is the pick for a traditional face, and the Reizen Talking LCD Alarm Cube Clock for a visible screen. No pick wins every category, so the right one depends on the user.

howToChoose.intro: These two designs solve different problems, so it helps to know which problem you have.

cards.label: Atomic clocks
cards.text: An atomic clock listens for a daily radio signal and corrects its own time, so it stays right without help. The Reizen Talking Atomic Alarm Clock and the Reizen Talking Atomic Analog Alarm Clock both work this way. Choose these if nobody will be around to reset the clock, and place them where the signal can reach.

cards.label: Cube clocks
cards.text: A cube clock packs its functions into a small block that sits on a table and speaks on demand. The Reizen 3-in-1 Talking Super Cube Clock adds a calendar and timer, while the Reizen Talking LCD Alarm Cube Clock adds a visible screen. Choose these if you want extra functions or a display and can reset the time by hand when needed.

howToChoose.note: Pick atomic if reliability is the priority, and a cube if the extra functions are the point.

howToChoose.subheading: For Gifting to a Parent Specifically
howToChoose.intro: A clock that is hard to set up quickly becomes a clock that sits in a drawer.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a clock with a button the user can find without looking, a voice they say is easy to understand, and a setup you can do for them in one visit. Make sure the language matches the listener and that the power source is one you can maintain from afar. Avoid models with many functions unless the person has asked for them.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Reizen Extra Large Button Talking Alarm Clock is the simplest gift because one press does the main job. The Reizen Talking Atomic Alarm Clock is the best gift for someone who lives alone, since it resets itself. The Reizen Talking Atomic Analog Alarm Clock suits a parent who loves a traditional dial, and the Reizen 3-in-1 Talking Super Cube Clock suits one who likes timers.

howToChoose.intro: Stepping up costs more, but only some upgrades remove real daily friction.

faq.q: Which Reizen talking clock is easiest to use?
faq.a: The Reizen Extra Large Button Talking Alarm Clock is the simplest, because one big white button speaks the time and a second press speaks the date. The body is only 3.50 inches across, so there is little to find or misread. If the listener also wants automatic correction, the Reizen Talking Atomic Alarm Clock is the next easiest to live with.

faq.q: Do I need an atomic clock?
faq.a: You do not need one, but it is worth having if nobody will reset the clock after a power cut or a daylight saving change. The Reizen Talking Atomic Alarm Clock and the Reizen Talking Atomic Analog Alarm Clock both receive a daily radio signal. If a relative visits often, a hand-set model works fine and keeps things simpler.

faq.q: How do I pick between the two cube clocks?
faq.a: Choose the Reizen 3-in-1 Talking Super Cube Clock if you want a talking calendar and a countdown timer, and its dual voice feature is a bonus. Choose the Reizen Talking LCD Alarm Cube Clock if you want a readable screen and a beep or voice alarm. Both sit on a tabletop, so the decision comes down to extras versus display.

faq.q: Can the voice or language be changed?
faq.a: Only some models list a voice choice, such as the dual voice feature on the Reizen 3-in-1 Talking Super Cube Clock. Language is usually fixed by the version you buy, so a Spanish clock will speak Spanish. Read the full title of the listing before ordering to avoid an easy mistake.

faq.q: Will hourly announcements keep someone awake?
faq.a: The optional hourly report on the Reizen Talking Atomic Alarm Clock runs from 8am to 10pm, so it stops in the late evening and overnight. Even so, a bedside clock that speaks on the hour can still disturb a light sleeper. If that is a worry, turn the option off or place the clock across the room.

faq.q: Is a touch button harder to use than a physical one?
faq.a: For many people it is, because a touch surface gives less feedback than a raised key. The Reizen Talking Atomic Analog Alarm Clock uses a touch button, so people with reduced fingertip feeling should try it first. The Reizen Extra Large Button Talking Alarm Clock uses a big physical button and is the safer option for that situation.

faq.q: What should I check before gifting one?
faq.a: Check the language of the voice, how the clock is powered, and whether the time can be set without help. Then set it up yourself during a visit and write down the steps for the listener. Finally, keep the receipt, since the Reizen Talking Atomic Analog Alarm Clock lists a 90-day warranty.
